newsitem.title: UK: North Sea wet crude eases lower, awaits US buying.
newsitem.headline: North Sea wet crude eases lower, awaits US buying.

text.p: Differentials for North Sea crudes eased back slightly on Wednesday, with sellers hoping for an upturn in transatlantic trade to support prices for remaining January barrels.
While some three million barrels of Norwegian crude and one million barrels of Brent have been fixed to move to the United States in the second decade, no third decade vessels have yet been fixed.
"The arb is still open on paper but we need to see a bit more interest on the buying side," a trader said.
Local buying interest was said to be relaxed.
An Ekofisk cargo loading Jan 23 was traded in the morning at Dated Brent +22 cents, three cents down on Tuesday's trade, while a Jan 28-30 cargo later fetched just Dated +18 cents.
A Gullfaks cargo loading Jan 22-24 traded at Dated Brent +30 cents.
There was only one Brent cargo, loading Jan 23-25, passing through the paper chains on Wednesday. Including this cargo, there are 13 Brents scheduled to load by the end of the month.
Brent intermonth spreads eased lower with discussion slack. Jan/Feb was talked at +27/+31 cents, with Feb/Mar at +50/+54.

Feb Brent paper was trading about 19 cents lower at $24.40 a barrel at 1600 GMT, in line with IPE screen levels. Values dropped down to the low $24.20s earlier on the back of bearish weekly stocks data from the United States.
CFDs for next week held steady while Jan 20-24 dates firmed slightly to trade at March Brent +45 and +47 cents.
